exam_name: AWS Certified Generative AI Developer - Professional

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which Amazon Bedrock runtime API offers a single message-based request format that works across many chat models, so application code does not need a different request body for each model provider?

options.A: The GetFoundationModelAvailability API
options.B: The CreateModelCustomizationJob API
options.C: The Converse API
options.D: The ListFoundationModels API

questions.explanation: The Converse API uses a unified messages structure across supporting models, whereas InvokeModel requires each model's native request body. The other calls manage or list models rather than run inference.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: In the Converse API, which inference configuration field limits how many tokens the model may generate in its reply?

options.A: guardrailConfig
options.B: topK
options.C: stopSequences
options.D: maxTokens

questions.explanation: maxTokens caps the length of the generated response. stopSequences ends generation on a matching string, and topK narrows sampling candidates; neither sets a length cap.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does the top-p (nucleus sampling) parameter control when a model chooses the next token?

options.A: It sets the maximum number of tokens the model is allowed to accept in the prompt
options.B: It controls how many times a failed request is automatically retried by the SDK
options.C: It chooses how many few-shot examples are placed ahead of the user's question
options.D: It restricts sampling to the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p

questions.explanation: Top-p keeps only the most probable tokens whose combined probability reaches the threshold and samples from that set. It has nothing to do with input limits, examples or retries.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: A prompt gives the model only an instruction and the input text, with no worked examples. Which prompting style is this?

options.A: Zero-shot prompting
options.B: Few-shot prompting
options.C: Prompt chaining
options.D: Retrieval-augmented prompting

questions.explanation: Zero-shot prompting relies on the instruction alone. Few-shot adds demonstrations, and chaining splits work across several prompts.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which prompting technique asks the model to lay out intermediate reasoning steps before it gives its final answer?

options.A: Negative-weight prompting
options.B: Embedding-based prompting
options.C: Chain-of-thought prompting
options.D: Stop-sequence prompting

questions.explanation: Chain-of-thought prompting elicits step-by-step reasoning, which often improves accuracy on multi-step problems.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: An application must answer questions about screenshots of dashboards that users upload. Which model characteristic is required?

options.A: An embedding model with 1,024 output dimensions
options.B: Support for image input, that is, a multimodal model
options.C: A text-only model with the largest available context window
options.D: A model that only produces images as output

questions.explanation: Interpreting screenshots requires a model that accepts images as input. A text-only model cannot read them regardless of its context size.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: In Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management, how are the parts of a saved prompt template that change at runtime represented?

options.A: As CloudWatch metric dimensions that are attached to every invocation record
options.B: As IAM policy conditions that the model evaluates before generating any text
options.C: As variables written in double curly braces, filled in when the prompt is invoked
options.D: As separate embedding vectors stored alongside the template in a vector index

questions.explanation: Prompt templates use variables such as {{customer_name}} that are replaced with real values at invocation time.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does Amazon Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing do?

options.A: It rewrites every incoming prompt into another language before it reaches the model
options.B: It saves prompts in a vector index so that similar prompts can be reused later
options.C: It fine-tunes the chosen model after every request using the latest user feedback
options.D: It sends each request to a model within a family based on predicted response quality and cost

questions.explanation: Intelligent Prompt Routing predicts which model in a family can handle a given prompt well and routes accordingly, balancing quality against cost and latency.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Why do many prompt guides recommend wrapping user-supplied text in delimiters such as XML-style tags?

options.A: To make clear which part is data and which part is instructions
options.B: To switch the model into a special fine-tuned mode for that part of the input
options.C: To make the model run noticeably faster when it processes very long inputs
options.D: To reduce the number of billed tokens to zero for the wrapped section

questions.explanation: Delimiters separate untrusted or variable data from the instructions, which improves reliability and helps limit prompt injection.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock API returns relevant source chunks for a query without calling a foundation model to write an answer?

options.A: StartIngestionJob
options.B: RetrieveAndGenerate
options.C: InvokeAgent
options.D: Retrieve

questions.explanation: Retrieve returns only the matching chunks and scores. RetrieveAndGenerate also calls a model to compose the answer.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which Knowledge Bases API retrieves relevant chunks and then has a foundation model produce a grounded answer with citations in one call?

options.A: ListIngestionJobs
options.B: GetKnowledgeBase
options.C: RetrieveAndGenerate
options.D: Retrieve

questions.explanation: RetrieveAndGenerate combines retrieval and generation and returns citations that point back to source chunks.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: New documents were uploaded to the S3 bucket behind a Bedrock knowledge base data source. What must be done before they can appear in query results?

options.A: Recreate the knowledge base from scratch
options.B: Restart the foundation model endpoint
options.C: Create a new IAM user for each document
options.D: Run a data source sync (start an ingestion job)

questions.explanation: Knowledge bases index content during an ingestion job, so changes in S3 become searchable only after a sync.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Semantic chunking in a Bedrock knowledge base splits documents based on what?

options.A: A fixed number of characters, cutting through sentences wherever the limit falls
options.B: The file size of each object stored in the Amazon S3 data source bucket
options.C: The alphabetical order of the words that appear in each document section
options.D: Shifts in meaning between adjacent sentences, so each chunk stays topically coherent

questions.explanation: Semantic chunking groups sentences by meaning rather than by a fixed length, which keeps related ideas together.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the main benefit of returning citations with a RAG answer?

options.A: Embedding costs are removed from the bill for every request that cites
options.B: The model no longer needs any retrieved context to answer the question
options.C: The context window becomes unlimited for any conversation that has citations
options.D: Users can check the answer against the source passages it drew from

questions.explanation: Citations tie statements to retrieved sources, which supports verification and trust.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A knowledge base must ingest PDFs full of tables and diagrams. Which parsing option is designed to handle that kind of complex content better than default text extraction?

options.A: Removing all tables before ingestion
options.B: Using a foundation model as the document parser
options.C: Splitting each PDF on every space character
options.D: Renaming the files with a .txt extension

questions.explanation: Bedrock knowledge bases can use a foundation model to parse complex documents, extracting tables, figures and layout that default parsing may miss.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A business team wants to ask natural language questions of data that lives in Amazon Redshift tables. Which Knowledge Bases capability fits?

options.A: Fixed-size chunking applied to the Redshift storage files themselves
options.B: Reranking of unstructured PDF passages returned by a keyword search
options.C: Structured data retrieval, which translates the question into SQL
options.D: A denied topic policy attached to the Redshift cluster endpoint

questions.explanation: Structured data retrieval turns natural language into SQL against supported structured stores such as Amazon Redshift, instead of embedding table contents.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which AWS service can a Bedrock knowledge base use as a graph store to support GraphRAG?

options.A: AWS Certificate Manager
options.B: Amazon Neptune Analytics
options.C: Amazon Simple Queue Service
options.D: Amazon Route 53 hosted zones

questions.explanation: GraphRAG in Knowledge Bases builds relationships between entities and stores them in Amazon Neptune Analytics to improve multi-hop retrieval.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which two formats can define the interface of an action group in a Bedrock Agent?

options.A: A CSV file or a Parquet file
options.B: A CloudFormation stack or an AMI
options.C: An OpenAPI schema or function details
options.D: A Dockerfile or a Helm chart

questions.explanation: Action groups describe callable operations with either an OpenAPI schema or a function definition, so the agent knows what parameters to supply.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What does the return of control option do for a Bedrock Agent action?

options.A: It stops the agent permanently and deletes the session and its stored state
options.B: It hands the action parameters back to the calling application, which runs the action itself
options.C: It moves the agent into another AWS Region so that the action runs closer to users
options.D: It disables guardrails for the current turn so the action can finish faster

questions.explanation: Return of control lets the client application execute an action and send the result back, instead of having the agent invoke a Lambda function.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is an agent alias in Amazon Bedrock Agents?

options.A: A CloudWatch alarm that pauses the agent whenever its error rate rises
options.B: A pointer to a specific agent version that applications call for stable deployments
options.C: A second foundation model attached to the agent so that it can fail over if needed
options.D: A vector index in which the agent stores the history of every conversation

questions.explanation: Applications invoke an alias, which references an agent version, so they can switch versions without changing client code.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which Bedrock runtime API is used by an application to send a user request to an agent and stream back its response?

options.A: InvokeAgent
options.B: CreateAgent
options.C: PrepareAgent
options.D: UpdateAgentAlias

questions.explanation: InvokeAgent, part of the Bedrock Agents runtime, runs the agent for one turn. The other calls create or manage agents and are build-time operations.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the purpose of enabling trace on an agent invocation?

options.A: To see the agent's intermediate reasoning, tool calls and observations for debugging
options.B: To convert the agent into a knowledge base for later use
options.C: To speed up the agent by skipping its orchestration step for repeated requests
options.D: To encrypt the final response with a customer managed KMS key

questions.explanation: Trace output exposes each orchestration step, which helps diagnose why an agent chose a particular action.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What does the code interpreter capability let a Bedrock Agent do?

options.A: Give the agent unrestricted shell access to resources inside your VPC
options.B: Translate the agent's instructions into another language for global users
options.C: Write and run code in a secure sandbox, for example to perform calculations or analyze data
options.D: Compile and deploy the agent's Lambda functions automatically after each change

questions.explanation: The code interpreter runs model-generated code in an isolated sandbox, which is useful for math, data analysis and chart generation.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: In Amazon Bedrock multi-agent collaboration, what is the role of the supervisor agent?

options.A: It stores the embeddings of every collaborator agent in a shared vector index
options.B: It breaks down the task and delegates parts to collaborator agents, then combines their results
options.C: It replaces IAM by deciding which collaborator agents are authorized to run
options.D: It only measures the response latency of each collaborator agent and reports it

questions.explanation: The supervisor decomposes a request, routes work to specialized collaborators and consolidates their outputs into a final response.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is Amazon Bedrock AgentCore designed for?

options.A: Storing curated training datasets and launching fine-tuning jobs for foundation models
options.B: Replacing Amazon S3 as the primary object store for documents and model artifacts
options.C: Managing DNS records and TLS certificates for agent endpoints across accounts
options.D: Deploying and operating AI agents securely at scale with managed runtime, memory and tool access services

questions.explanation: AgentCore provides managed building blocks such as runtime, memory, gateway, identity and observability for production agents, regardless of framework.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2 lets you choose the output vector size. Which set lists sizes it supports?

options.B: 2, 4 or 8 dimensions
options.C: Only a single fixed size of 3 dimensions
options.D: 256, 512 or 1,024 dimensions

questions.explanation: Titan Text Embeddings V2 offers configurable output dimensions of 256, 512 and 1,024, trading storage and speed against accuracy.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: A team has thousands of scanned invoices as image PDFs. Which service extracts text, tables and form fields so the content can be embedded?

options.A: AWS Direct Connect
options.B: Amazon Textract
options.C: Amazon Polly
options.D: Amazon Lex

questions.explanation: Textract performs OCR and structured extraction on scanned documents. Polly produces speech and Lex builds conversational bots.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Call-center recordings need to be searchable through a RAG application. Which service should convert the audio to text first?

options.A: AWS Glue DataBrew
options.B: Amazon Translate
options.C: Amazon Transcribe
options.D: Amazon Rekognition

questions.explanation: Transcribe converts speech to text, which can then be chunked and embedded. Rekognition analyzes images and video.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which PostgreSQL extension lets Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL store embeddings and run similarity queries?

options.A: pg_cron
options.B: postgis_topology
options.C: pgvector
options.D: pg_stat_statements

questions.explanation: pgvector adds a vector data type and distance operators, making Aurora PostgreSQL usable as a vector store.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is Amazon S3 Vectors?

options.A: Vector storage in S3 with native APIs to store and query embeddings cost-effectively
options.B: A tool that converts objects in S3 into image thumbnails for a media catalog
options.C: A billing report that breaks down S3 request charges by vector-shaped tags
options.D: A replication feature that copies S3 buckets between AWS accounts automatically

questions.explanation: S3 Vectors adds purpose-built vector storage and query support to S3, aimed at lower-cost, large-scale vector data.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Why must the same embedding model be used to embed both the documents and the user's query?

options.A: Because the vector database only accepts a single IAM role for all read and write calls
options.B: Because queries are always billed at the same rate as the indexed documents
options.C: Vectors from different models live in different spaces, so distances between them are meaningless
options.D: Because the chunk size is stored inside the weights of the embedding model

questions.explanation: Similarity search only works when both vectors come from the same embedding space.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which AWS service is a serverless ETL service commonly used to clean and transform data before it is chunked and embedded?

options.A: AWS Shield
options.B: AWS Glue
options.C: Amazon CloudFront
options.D: Amazon Inspector

questions.explanation: AWS Glue runs serverless ETL jobs to cleanse, join and reshape data into the form an embedding pipeline needs.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: How can you tag documents so a knowledge base can filter results by attributes such as department or year?

options.A: Encrypt each document with a different KMS key that encodes its attributes
options.B: Place a CloudWatch alarm on each document to record the department name
options.C: Add a metadata file next to each source document in S3 that lists the attributes
options.D: Rename each S3 bucket after the department so that queries can target the bucket

questions.explanation: A metadata file alongside a source object provides attributes that queries can use as filters during retrieval.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: In Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock, what does a denied topic policy do?

options.A: It deletes a topic from the knowledge base index once users stop asking about it
options.B: It lowers the sampling temperature whenever a chosen topic is being discussed
options.C: It blocks user inputs and model responses that fall under topics you define in natural language
options.D: It restricts which IAM users are allowed to read a topic's invocation logs

questions.explanation: Denied topics let you describe subject areas the application must not discuss, and the guardrail blocks matching prompts and responses.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which Guardrails capability detects personally identifiable information in prompts or responses and can mask or block it?

options.A: Sensitive information filters
options.B: Contextual grounding checks
options.C: Profanity word filters
options.D: Prompt cache checkpoints

questions.explanation: Sensitive information filters recognize PII types such as names, emails and card numbers, and can mask or block them.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What does the ApplyGuardrail API allow you to do?

options.A: Fine-tune a model on the blocked content so it stops producing it
options.B: Attach a guardrail directly to an S3 bucket policy for all objects
options.C: Create a new IAM role that the guardrail assumes when it runs
options.D: Evaluate text against a guardrail without invoking a foundation model

questions.explanation: ApplyGuardrail checks arbitrary input or output text independently of any model call, so it can protect content from any source.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What does a contextual grounding check in Guardrails evaluate?

options.A: Whether the prompt has been written in the same language as the documents
options.B: Whether the caller's IAM role is permitted to use the model in the current Region
options.C: Whether a response is supported by the source material and relevant to the user's query
options.D: Whether the embedding dimensions of the index match the embedding model output

questions.explanation: Contextual grounding checks score responses for grounding in the provided source and relevance to the question, helping catch hallucinations in RAG.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which guardrail filter is aimed at detecting jailbreak attempts and prompt injection in user input?

options.A: The PII entity filter
options.B: The prompt attack content filter
options.C: The response length limiter
options.D: The profanity word list

questions.explanation: Content filters include a prompt attack category that flags attempts to override or bypass the model's instructions.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: A workload in a private subnet must call Amazon Bedrock without sending traffic over the public internet. What should be configured?

options.A: An internet gateway with a public IP on the workload
options.B: A CloudFront distribution in front of Bedrock
options.C: A Route 53 public hosted zone
options.D: A VPC interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) for Bedrock

questions.explanation: Interface VPC endpoints let resources reach Bedrock over the AWS network with no internet path.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which is the best least-privilege approach for a Lambda function that only needs to call one specific foundation model?

options.A: Share one long-lived access key in an environment variable
options.B: Allow bedrock:* on all resources
options.C: Allow bedrock:InvokeModel only on that model's ARN
options.D: Attach AdministratorAccess to the function role

questions.explanation: Scoping the action and resource to the single model follows least privilege and limits the blast radius if credentials are misused.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which statement about customer data in Amazon Bedrock is accurate?

options.A: Bedrock always stores prompts in a public bucket
options.B: Your prompts and completions are not used to train the base foundation models
options.C: Every prompt is added to the public training set of the model
options.D: Your prompts are shared with all model providers by default

questions.explanation: AWS states that customer inputs and outputs in Bedrock are not used to train the base models and are not shared with model providers.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which AWS service can discover and classify sensitive data in S3 buckets before those files are ingested into a RAG pipeline?

options.A: Amazon Macie
options.B: Amazon Detective
options.C: AWS Config
options.D: Amazon GuardDuty

questions.explanation: Macie uses pattern matching and machine learning to find sensitive data such as PII in S3, so it can be cleaned or excluded before ingestion.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is Amazon Bedrock batch inference best suited for?

options.A: Testing IAM policies for the calling role before the application is deployed
options.B: Serving sub-second replies to users of a live chat widget on a website
options.C: Streaming tokens to a mobile app one at a time as they are produced
options.D: Processing a large set of prompts from S3 asynchronously when results are not needed immediately

questions.explanation: Batch inference reads many prompts from S3, writes results back to S3, and is typically priced lower than on-demand, making it ideal for offline jobs.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How does prompt caching reduce cost and latency in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: It removes the system prompt from every request after the first call
options.B: It skips guardrail evaluation for any request that repeats an earlier prompt
options.C: It reuses a previously processed prompt prefix instead of reprocessing it on every request
options.D: It stores the model's weights on the client device to avoid network calls

questions.explanation: When a long, stable prefix such as instructions or documents is cached, later requests reuse it, lowering input processing time and cost.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which Bedrock feature helps attribute model usage and cost to a specific application or team by using tags?

options.A: Guardrail versions
options.B: Model access approval requests
options.C: Knowledge base data sources
options.D: Application inference profiles

questions.explanation: Application inference profiles can carry cost allocation tags, enabling usage tracking per workload in Cost Explorer.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A Bedrock call returns a ThrottlingException. What is the recommended client-side response?

options.A: Delete the request and never retry
options.B: Retry immediately in a tight loop
options.C: Switch to a larger model automatically
options.D: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter

questions.explanation: Backing off with jitter spreads retries over time and avoids worsening throttling.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is the goal of model distillation in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: To train a smaller, cheaper model to mimic a larger model on your use case
options.B: To merge two unrelated models into one endpoint behind a single model ID
options.C: To raise the maximum context window that a hosted model can accept
options.D: To compress the training data so that it takes less space in Amazon S3

questions.explanation: Distillation uses a larger teacher model's outputs to fine-tune a smaller student, giving similar quality on the task at lower cost and latency.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A team fine-tunes a model in Amazon Bedrock. How is the resulting custom model typically served for inference?

options.A: Through an Amazon SQS queue that buffers each inference request
options.B: Through a shared on-demand endpoint that every customer in the Region uses
options.C: Through Provisioned Throughput purchased for that custom model
options.D: Through an S3 static website that hosts the model artifacts

questions.explanation: Custom models created with Bedrock fine-tuning or continued pre-training are generally invoked using Provisioned Throughput.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How are on-demand foundation model invocations in Amazon Bedrock generally billed?

options.A: By the number of input and output tokens processed
options.B: By the number of guardrails created
options.C: By the total size of the S3 bucket
options.D: By the number of IAM users in the account

questions.explanation: On-demand text models are priced per input token and per output token, so prompt and response length drive cost.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which CloudWatch metric for Bedrock rises when requests are being rejected because you exceeded a quota?

options.A: InvocationLatency
options.B: InvocationThrottles
options.C: InputTokenCount
options.D: OutputImageCount

questions.explanation: InvocationThrottles counts requests throttled by Bedrock, so a rise signals you are hitting rate or token limits.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which Bedrock runtime API returns a model's reply incrementally as it is generated, using the same unified message format as Converse?

options.A: GetPrompt
options.B: ListCustomModels
options.C: CreateModelInvocationJob
options.D: ConverseStream

questions.explanation: ConverseStream is the streaming counterpart of Converse, delivering tokens as they are produced. The other calls do not run interactive inference.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: In Amazon Bedrock Prompt Management, what does creating a prompt version accomplish?

options.A: It permanently attaches the prompt to a guardrail and locks both
options.B: It automatically retrains the model on the text of the saved prompt
options.C: It replicates the prompt into every AWS Region in the account
options.D: It saves an immutable snapshot of the prompt that applications can reference reliably

questions.explanation: A version freezes the current draft so production code can pin to a known, unchanging prompt while you keep editing the draft.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What is role prompting?

options.A: Assigning the model a persona or expertise, such as "You are a senior tax accountant", to shape tone and content
options.B: Rotating the credentials that the model uses on a fixed schedule for security
options.C: Letting each end user choose which foundation model will answer their question
options.D: Assigning an IAM role to every token in a prompt so that access is checked per word

questions.explanation: Role prompting gives the model an identity and perspective that steers the style, vocabulary and level of detail of its answers.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Which guideline generally produces more reliable prompts?

options.A: State clearly and specifically what the model should do and the format you want
options.B: Keep instructions vague so the model can decide the task and format by itself
options.C: Only list what the model must never do and leave the desired behavior unstated
options.D: Write all instructions as one long sentence without any punctuation or structure

questions.explanation: Clear, specific positive instructions with an explicit output format tend to give more consistent results than vague or purely negative ones.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: Besides model quality, which factor most directly affects the cost of a single on-demand request?

options.A: The per-token price of the model and the number of input and output tokens
options.B: The number of browser tabs that are open in the playground at the same time
options.C: The color scheme that has been selected for the Bedrock console interface
options.D: The display name that was given to the saved prompt template

questions.explanation: On-demand pricing is per token, so both the model's rate and the lengths of the prompt and response set the cost.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What is the Amazon Bedrock playground used for?

options.A: Trying prompts and models interactively in the console without writing code
options.B: Exporting CloudTrail logs to Amazon S3 on a daily schedule
options.C: Provisioning GPU instances for training a custom foundation model from scratch
options.D: Managing the identity providers that are connected to the AWS account

questions.explanation: Playgrounds let you experiment with models, parameters and prompts interactively to compare behavior before building an application.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does tool use (function calling) in the Converse API enable?

options.A: The model can request a call to a tool you define and return structured arguments for it
options.B: The model can install software packages directly on your application servers
options.C: The model can edit the IAM policy of the caller to grant itself more access
options.D: The model can change its own weights during the course of a chat session

questions.explanation: With tool use, you describe tools in the request, the model responds with the tool name and arguments, and your code runs the tool and returns the result.

questions.domain: Foundation Model Selection and Prompt Engineering
questions.question: What does a model's context window limit?

options.A: The number of Regions in which the model can be made available to customers
options.B: The total number of tokens the model can handle in a request, covering the prompt and generated output
options.C: The number of guardrails that can be attached to a single model invocation
options.D: The number of AWS accounts that are permitted to call the model in one day

questions.explanation: The context window bounds how much text, measured in tokens, the model can consider at once, including what it generates.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: A knowledge base needs custom logic to split and clean documents in a way the built-in strategies do not support. What can be used?

options.A: A CloudFront function that is attached to the S3 bucket holding the documents
options.B: A custom transformation using an AWS Lambda function during ingestion
options.C: A Route 53 health check that runs against the knowledge base endpoint
options.D: An SNS topic that the knowledge base subscribes to for every new object

questions.explanation: Knowledge bases support custom transformation Lambda functions to change how documents are chunked or processed before indexing.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Which of the following can be used as a data source for a Bedrock knowledge base besides Amazon S3?

options.A: An AWS CloudFormation stack policy
options.B: A web crawler pointed at public web pages
options.C: An Amazon SQS dead-letter queue
options.D: An EC2 instance's boot disk

questions.explanation: Bedrock knowledge bases offer connectors such as web crawler, Confluence, SharePoint and Salesforce in addition to S3.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What is the purpose of the service role you supply when creating a Bedrock knowledge base?

options.A: It allows Bedrock to read the data source and write to the vector store on your behalf
options.B: It decides which foundation model each end user prefers to work with
options.C: It encrypts prompts on the client before they are sent to the service
options.D: It signs end users in to the chat interface that sits in front of the knowledge base

questions.explanation: The knowledge base service role grants Bedrock the permissions to access S3, call the embedding model and write to the vector store.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: In a RetrieveAndGenerate prompt template, which placeholder is replaced with the retrieved passages?

options.A: $model_identifier$
options.B: $service_role_arn$
options.C: $search_results$
options.D: $source_bucket$

questions.explanation: Knowledge base prompt templates use $search_results$ for retrieved content and $query$ for the user's question.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: What does a reranker do after the initial vector retrieval in a Bedrock knowledge base?

options.A: Encrypts each retrieved chunk with a second key before it reaches the model
options.B: Deletes any chunks that are older than one day from the vector index
options.C: Re-scores the retrieved chunks against the query so the most relevant ones come first
options.D: Re-embeds the entire corpus with a newer embedding model on a nightly schedule

questions.explanation: Rerank models score query and chunk pairs more precisely than vector similarity alone, improving the ordering of results passed to the model.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: When is the "no chunking" option reasonable for a knowledge base data source?

options.A: When the source data in S3 is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key
options.B: When you want the smallest possible index regardless of retrieval relevance
options.C: When each file is already small and prepared so that one file should be one chunk
options.D: When documents are very large books that need to be split into many pieces

questions.explanation: With no chunking, each file becomes a single chunk, which suits content already split into appropriately sized units.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: After a data source sync finishes, where can you check how many documents were scanned, indexed or failed?

options.A: In the IAM credential report for the knowledge base service role
options.B: In the Route 53 query log for the private hosted zone
options.C: In the ingestion job details and statistics
options.D: In the AWS Health Dashboard under the billing tab

questions.explanation: Each ingestion job reports statistics such as documents scanned, indexed and failed, which helps identify content that did not make it into the index.

questions.domain: RAG and Knowledge Base Design
questions.question: Amazon Kendra can act as which component in a RAG solution?

options.A: An intelligent enterprise search retriever that returns relevant passages for the model
options.B: The load balancer that sits in front of the Lambda function
options.C: The foundation model that writes the final answer that users see
options.D: The IAM policy evaluator that decides which users may see each result

questions.explanation: Kendra provides ML-powered search across enterprise content and can supply relevant passages as context for generation.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What do Amazon Bedrock Flows provide?

options.A: A network flow log that records traffic between subnets in a VPC
options.B: A queue that buffers every model response until the client is ready
options.C: A billing report that tracks the flow of tokens between accounts
options.D: A visual way to link prompts, knowledge bases, Lambda functions and other steps into a workflow

questions.explanation: Bedrock Flows lets you compose generative AI workflows as connected nodes, such as prompts, knowledge bases and code steps, and invoke them through an API.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the agent's instruction field used for?

options.A: Describing in natural language what the agent should do and how it should behave
options.B: Holding the encryption keys that the agent uses for its session data
options.C: Listing the IP address ranges that are allowed to call the agent
options.D: Specifying the vector dimensions of the embeddings the agent creates

questions.explanation: The instruction tells the agent's underlying model its purpose, tone and constraints, and strongly influences orchestration decisions.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: How does an agent gain access to company documents for answering questions?

options.A: By attaching an EBS volume to the agent
options.B: By giving the agent root credentials
options.C: By copying documents into the agent's alias name
options.D: By associating one or more knowledge bases with the agent

questions.explanation: An agent can be linked to knowledge bases, which it queries when it decides that retrieved information is needed to respond.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: An action group Lambda function must be invokable by a Bedrock Agent. What permission must be in place?

options.A: A resource-based policy on the function that allows the Bedrock service principal to invoke it
options.B: A public function URL that has no authentication so that Bedrock can reach it
options.C: A bucket policy attached to the agent's alias that lists allowed callers
options.D: An SQS queue policy that is created separately for each user session

questions.explanation: Bedrock needs permission to invoke the Lambda function, granted through a resource-based policy scoped to the agent.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What does agent memory allow across separate conversations?

options.A: The agent can rewrite its own OpenAPI schema between conversations
options.B: The agent can grow its context window without any limit on tokens
options.C: The agent can retain summaries of prior sessions for the same user identifier
options.D: The agent can skip authentication on later calls from the same user

questions.explanation: Memory retention summarizes past sessions and makes them available in later conversations for the same memory ID, supporting continuity.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is an inline agent in Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: An agent whose instructions, tools and knowledge bases are defined at invocation time in the request
options.B: An agent that runs only inside a single Lambda function and cannot call tools
options.C: An agent that is stored as a local file on the developer's laptop
options.D: An agent that cannot use any foundation model for its reasoning steps

questions.explanation: Inline agents let you supply the configuration dynamically with each InvokeInlineAgent request, rather than pre-creating an agent resource.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: Which agent setting can require an end user to approve an action before the agent runs it?

options.A: A higher sampling temperature setting
options.B: User confirmation on an action group function
options.C: A shorter name for the agent alias
options.D: A larger chunk size for the knowledge base

questions.explanation: Action groups can be configured to request confirmation from the user before invoking a function, adding a human check on sensitive operations.

questions.domain: Agentic Workflows with Bedrock Agents
questions.question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

options.A: A method for compressing model weights so that they load faster
options.B: An open protocol that standardizes how AI applications connect to tools and data sources
options.C: A proprietary file format for storing embeddings in Amazon S3 buckets
options.D: A protocol that meters and bills model usage for each customer account

questions.explanation: MCP defines a common way for models and agents to discover and call external tools and data, reducing custom integration work.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which similarity measure compares vectors based on the angle between them rather than their lengths?

options.A: Manhattan clock time
options.B: Cosine similarity
options.C: Hamming distance
options.D: Levenshtein distance

questions.explanation: Cosine similarity measures directional alignment of vectors, which makes it a common choice for text embeddings.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Why do vector databases use approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) algorithms such as HNSW?

options.A: To find close vectors quickly at scale by trading a small amount of accuracy for speed
options.B: To guarantee that exact matches are always returned with no error at all
options.C: To encrypt the stored vectors while they are at rest in the index
options.D: To convert stored vectors back into the original source text on demand

questions.explanation: ANN indexes such as HNSW avoid comparing against every vector, which keeps search fast on large collections with a small recall trade-off.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: When you create an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection to back a knowledge base, which collection type should you choose?

options.A: Time series
options.B: Vector search
options.C: Search on document titles only
options.D: Log analytics

questions.explanation: The vector search collection type is designed for storing embeddings and serving similarity queries.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: The vector index dimension is 1,024 but the embedding model outputs 512-dimensional vectors. What is the likely result?

options.A: The index resizes itself automatically with no effect on indexing
options.B: Search becomes faster and more accurate because of the extra dimensions
options.C: The embedding model switches itself to 1,024 dimensions on its own
options.D: Indexing fails or is rejected because the dimensions do not match

questions.explanation: The index dimension must equal the embedding model's output size, otherwise writes are rejected.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: What is the key capability of a multimodal embedding model such as Amazon Titan Multimodal Embeddings?

options.A: It generates new images from text prompts using a diffusion model
options.B: It transcribes speech in video files into text for indexing
options.C: It maps text and images into the same vector space so they can be searched together
options.D: It translates text between languages before the vectors are stored

questions.explanation: Multimodal embeddings place different data types in a shared space, enabling text-to-image and image-to-image similarity search.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Which AWS service offers in-memory vector search suited to very low-latency retrieval?

options.A: Amazon EFS
options.B: AWS Snowball
options.C: Amazon Glacier
options.D: Amazon MemoryDB

questions.explanation: MemoryDB supports vector search over in-memory data, giving single-digit millisecond latency for applications that need it.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: Why should duplicate documents be removed before indexing them for RAG?

options.A: Duplicates are not permitted in Amazon S3 buckets
options.B: Duplicates create redundant chunks that crowd out diverse results and add cost
options.C: Duplicates make the generated embeddings invalid and unusable
options.D: Duplicates automatically disable all metadata filters on the index

questions.explanation: Duplicate content fills the top results with the same information and raises storage and embedding costs without adding value.

questions.domain: Data Preparation, Embeddings, and Vector Stores
questions.question: A team replaces its embedding model with a different one. What must they do with existing indexed content?

options.A: Nothing, because vectors are model independent
options.B: Keep the old vectors and only embed new queries
options.C: Delete the source documents
options.D: Re-embed and re-index the content with the new model

questions.explanation: Vectors from different models are not comparable, so the corpus must be re-embedded to match the new query embeddings.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is a word filter in Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock used for?

options.A: Compressing long words into shorter tokens to reduce the cost of each request
options.B: Spell-checking the model's answers before they are returned to the user
options.C: Blocking specific words or phrases, such as profanity or competitor names, in inputs and outputs
options.D: Translating the words in each prompt into the language of the model

questions.explanation: Word filters block exact terms or phrases you list, in addition to a managed profanity list.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which are categories of the content filters in Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock?

options.A: Hate, insults, sexual content, violence and misconduct
options.B: Read, write, list, delete and tag object operations
options.C: Latency, throughput, cost, availability and quota limits
options.D: Compute, storage, networking, database and analytics

questions.explanation: Content filters screen harmful categories such as hate, insults, sexual, violence and misconduct, with adjustable strength for inputs and outputs.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What is the difference between the DRAFT and a numbered guardrail version?

options.A: They are identical and can be used interchangeably in any environment
options.B: DRAFT is enforced in production, and versions are used for testing only
options.C: A version can be edited freely, but DRAFT is locked once created
options.D: DRAFT is the editable working copy, and a version is an immutable snapshot used in production

questions.explanation: You iterate on the DRAFT and create a version to lock the configuration, so production applications reference a stable policy.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which Converse API request field attaches a guardrail to a model call?

options.A: guardrailConfig
options.B: additionalModelRequestFields
options.C: toolConfig
options.D: inferenceConfig

questions.explanation: guardrailConfig specifies the guardrail identifier and version applied to the request and response. The other fields control sampling, tools and model-specific options.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What does Amazon Bedrock model invocation logging capture when it is enabled?

options.A: The pricing details of the other customers that use the same model
options.B: Request and response data for model calls, delivered to CloudWatch Logs or S3
options.C: The internal weights of the foundation model that handled the request
options.D: The private keys of the users who call the models through the console

questions.explanation: Invocation logging is off by default and, when enabled, records prompts, completions and metadata to your chosen destination for auditing and analysis.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which trust relationship is required on the IAM service role that Bedrock assumes, for example to read your S3 training data?

options.A: No trust policy is needed because service roles are trusted by default
options.B: A trust policy that names the end user's email address as the principal
options.C: A trust policy that allows the bedrock.amazonaws.com service principal to assume the role
options.D: A trust policy that allows every AWS account to assume the role freely

questions.explanation: Service roles must trust the Bedrock service principal so it can assume the role and act with the permissions attached.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which AWS capability helps detect bias in data and models and explain model behavior?

options.A: Amazon Route 53 Resolver
options.B: Amazon SageMaker Clarify
options.C: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler
options.D: AWS Transit Gateway

questions.explanation: SageMaker Clarify provides bias detection and explainability metrics, supporting responsible AI reviews.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: Which service lets you add human review workflows for model outputs that need a person to check them?

options.A: Amazon Augmented AI (Amazon A2I)
options.B: AWS Backup vault lock
options.C: Amazon Cognito user pools
options.D: Amazon Pinpoint campaigns

questions.explanation: A2I provides human review loops, which suit high-stakes decisions where a person should confirm or correct model output.

questions.domain: Guardrails, Responsible AI, Security, and IAM
questions.question: What do Automated Reasoning checks in Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock validate?

options.A: Whether the weights of the foundation model have changed since the last release
options.B: Whether a response is consistent with formal rules or policies derived from your documents
options.C: Whether the S3 bucket that holds the source documents is publicly readable
options.D: Whether the password used by the end user meets the complexity policy

questions.explanation: Automated Reasoning checks apply logic-based verification against a policy you define to catch responses that contradict the rules.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How does LLM-as-a-judge model evaluation in Amazon Bedrock score outputs?

options.A: A separate evaluator model rates responses against metrics such as correctness or helpfulness
options.B: The AWS Billing service assigns quality scores based on token spend
options.C: The model rates its own output using an internal score stored in its weights
options.D: A human reviewer must read and rate every single response by hand

questions.explanation: Bedrock Evaluations can use a judge model to score generated responses on chosen metrics, giving faster, cheaper assessment than fully human review.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which is a sensible CloudWatch alarm for detecting Bedrock service-side problems?

options.A: An alarm on the color theme that is selected in the console
options.B: An alarm on the number of IAM users in the account
options.C: An alarm on InvocationServerErrors exceeding a threshold
options.D: An alarm on the length of the name of the saved prompt

questions.explanation: InvocationServerErrors counts 5xx responses, so alarming on it flags service-side failures that need attention.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: You enabled invocation logging to CloudWatch Logs and want to find the prompts that used the most tokens. What can you use?

options.A: AWS Artifact reports that are generated for compliance audits
options.B: AWS Trusted Advisor checks for open security groups
options.C: Amazon Macie classification jobs that scan the log bucket
options.D: CloudWatch Logs Insights queries on the invocation log group

questions.explanation: Logs Insights can query and aggregate the logged fields, such as token counts, to find expensive requests.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Which commitment terms are offered for Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput?

options.A: Only a single ten-year commitment that is paid up front
options.B: No commitment, a 1-month commitment, or a 6-month commitment
options.C: A commitment tied to one specific Availability Zone only
options.D: A commitment counted in the number of guardrails created

questions.explanation: Provisioned Throughput can be purchased with no commitment or with 1-month and 6-month terms, with longer terms priced lower per model unit.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: How does limiting the maximum output tokens help an application?

options.A: It improves the quality of the embeddings that are created
options.B: It increases the model's accuracy on every type of task it is given
options.C: It removes the need for guardrails on the model's responses
options.D: It bounds response length, which caps output cost and tail latency

questions.explanation: Setting a sensible maxTokens prevents runaway responses, reducing both the cost per request and the time to complete it.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Your workload keeps hitting Bedrock request quotas even with backoff. What is a supported next step?

options.A: Delete all of the guardrails that are currently attached
options.B: Rename the foundation model that the application calls
options.C: Create additional AWS accounts that use the same name and quotas
options.D: Request a quota increase through Service Quotas or AWS Support

questions.explanation: Quotas for tokens and requests per minute can be raised by request, and that is the intended path when steady demand exceeds the defaults.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: A chatbot receives many nearly identical questions. Which technique can cut cost and latency?

options.A: Semantic caching that returns a stored answer for sufficiently similar queries
options.B: Increasing the temperature so that answers become more varied
options.C: Disabling response streaming so tokens arrive in one block
options.D: Sending every question to the largest and most capable model

questions.explanation: Semantic caching compares the incoming question with earlier ones by embedding similarity and returns the saved answer, avoiding a model call.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: Why define generative AI infrastructure such as knowledge bases and agents with AWS CDK or CloudFormation?

options.A: It removes the need for IAM permissions on the resources
options.B: Deployments become repeatable, reviewable and consistent across environments
options.C: It makes foundation model usage free for the account
options.D: It disables CloudTrail logging for the deployed stack

questions.explanation: Infrastructure as code enables version control, code review and identical stacks in dev, test and production.

questions.domain: Deployment, Cost/Latency Optimization, Monitoring, and Troubleshooting
questions.question: What is Amazon SageMaker JumpStart useful for in a generative AI project?

options.A: Running interactive SQL queries directly over data stored in Amazon S3
options.B: Deploying and fine-tuning pre-trained foundation models on SageMaker endpoints you control
options.C: Managing Route 53 DNS records for internal and public endpoints of the application
options.D: Rotating database passwords for applications on a fixed schedule

questions.explanation: JumpStart offers a hub of pre-trained and open-weight models that you can deploy to SageMaker endpoints or fine-tune.
